scenarios.text:
CASE STUDY: Contoso GitHub Adoption

Contoso is moving several product teams from shared file folders to GitHub. The teams need a simple workflow for version control, branching, commits, pull requests, and repository visibility. Team members have different experience levels, so the solution must use GitHub fundamentals and clear collaboration practices.

CASE STUDY: Fabrikam Developer Platform

Fabrikam is standardizing its cloud development environment on GitHub. The organization wants repeatable development workspaces, basic automation, AI-assisted coding, and project tracking for feature delivery. The platform team must recommend beginner-friendly GitHub features that align with GH-900 level responsibilities.

CASE STUDY: Adventure Works Secure Collaboration

Adventure Works hosts internal and open-source repositories on GitHub. The company needs stronger repository governance, secure access, contributor guidance, and community health practices. Administrators want to use GitHub features that improve security, privacy, and sustainable collaboration without making the workflow unnecessarily complex.

questions.Question:
Contoso wants to track every meaningful change to application files and allow the team to return to earlier states.

Which concept provides this capability?

Options.reason: Incorrect. It distributes dependencies rather than tracking source history.
Correct. Version control records changes over time and supports review and recovery.
Incorrect. It publishes web content rather than managing change history.
Incorrect. It manages authentication rather than file revisions.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Version control is the foundation for tracking, comparing, and recovering changes in a project.

questions.Question:
A new user asks how Git differs from GitHub.

Which statement is most accurate?

Options.text: GitHub is the command-line replacement for Git.
Options.reason: Incorrect. GitHub does not replace Git as the underlying version control system.

Options.text: Git is a cloud-only GitHub plan for enterprises.
Options.reason: Incorrect. Git is not a GitHub subscription plan.

Options.text: GitHub is only used for issue tracking and cannot host code.
Options.reason: Incorrect. GitHub hosts repositories as a core capability.

Options.text: Git is a distributed version control system, while GitHub is a platform that hosts Git repositories and collaboration features.
Options.reason: Correct. This separates the local version control tool from the hosted collaboration service.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Git manages repository history; GitHub adds hosting, collaboration, automation, and governance features.

questions.Question:
Contoso needs an isolated line of development for a UI change without immediately affecting the main code line.

Which Git concept should the team use?

Options.reason: Correct. A branch lets work proceed independently before it is merged.
Incorrect. A release packages a version for distribution after work is complete.
Incorrect. A gist is for sharing snippets, not managing product development lines.
Incorrect. A license defines usage terms, not a line of development.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Branches support GitHub Flow by isolating changes until review and merge.

questions.Question:
A developer has changed three files locally and wants to record the changes in repository history with a message.

Which Git operation should be used?

Options.reason: Incorrect. A fork creates a copy of a repository under another account.
Incorrect. Watching controls notifications for repository activity.
Correct. A commit records staged changes as a point in history.
Incorrect. Starring bookmarks or shows interest in a repository.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: A commit is the unit of recorded change in Git history.

questions.Question:
Contoso wants a lightweight contribution model where developers branch, commit, open a pull request, review, and then merge.

Which workflow is being described?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Waterfall is a project methodology, not a GitHub branch workflow.
Correct. GitHub Flow uses branches and pull requests for collaborative changes.
Incorrect. GitHub Pages hosts static sites, not the end-to-end collaboration flow.
Incorrect. The dependency graph shows packages and dependencies.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Flow is the common GitHub collaboration workflow using branches and pull requests.

questions.Question:
A business analyst wants to format checklists, links, tables, and code snippets in issue comments.

Which syntax should they use?

Options.reason: Incorrect. YAML is commonly used for configuration files.
Incorrect. SCIM is used for identity provisioning.
Incorrect. CodeQL is used for semantic code analysis.
Correct. Markdown is used across GitHub for formatted communication.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Markdown helps users communicate clearly in issues, pull requests, READMEs, and discussions.

questions.Question:
A developer wants to work with repositories through a graphical desktop application instead of the command line.

Which GitHub product best fits this need?

Options.reason: Correct. GitHub Desktop provides a graphical client for common Git and GitHub tasks.
Incorrect. It provides security capabilities, not a local GUI client.
Incorrect. It executes automation jobs, not interactive repository management.
Incorrect. It supports funding maintainers, not desktop repository operations.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Desktop is appropriate for users who prefer a GUI for common Git workflows.

questions.Question:
A project manager wants to review notifications and participate in issues while away from a laptop.

Which option is designed for this mobile use case?

Options.reason: Incorrect. It is a self-hosted GitHub deployment option.
Incorrect. It hosts software packages.
Correct. GitHub Mobile supports reviewing and collaborating from mobile devices.
Incorrect. It provides cloud development environments.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Mobile is intended for on-the-go GitHub collaboration.

questions.Question: Which account type is best when multiple employees need shared ownership of repositories, teams, and permissions for a company?

Options.reason: Incorrect. A personal account represents an individual user.
Correct. An organization supports shared repositories, teams, roles, and centralized management.
Incorrect. A machine account is for automation patterns, not typical company ownership.
Incorrect. Gist is a feature, not an account type.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Organizations are used to manage collaborative work for teams and companies.

questions.Question:
A company requires centralized enterprise policies across many organizations.

Which GitHub construct is designed for this scale?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Topics classify repositories but do not manage policy.
Incorrect. Templates standardize issue creation.
Incorrect. Milestones group issues and pull requests for planning.
Correct. An enterprise account can manage policy and billing across organizations.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Enterprise accounts provide higher-level administration across organizations.

questions.Question:
A team member wants to download an existing repository and its history to a local machine for the first time.

Which Git operation should be used?

Options.reason: Correct. Cloning creates a local copy of an existing repository including history.
Incorrect. Merging combines changes from one branch into another.
Incorrect. Rebasing reapplies commits on another base.
Incorrect. A tag marks a specific point in history.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Clone is the initial action for creating a local working copy from a remote repository.

questions.Question:
A developer wants to upload local commits from a branch to the remote repository on GitHub.

Which Git operation should be used?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Pull retrieves remote changes into the local branch.
Incorrect. Status shows working tree state.
Correct. Push publishes local commits to a remote repository.
Incorrect. Blame shows line-level commit attribution.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Push sends local commits to the remote repository.

questions.Question:
A developer wants to bring remote changes into the current local branch and integrate them.

Which Git operation should be used?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Add stages changes for commit.
Correct. Pull fetches remote changes and integrates them into the current branch.
Incorrect. Init creates a new local Git repository.
Incorrect. Archive exports repository contents without normal collaboration history.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Pull is commonly used to update a local branch from its remote counterpart.

questions.Question:
A repository owner wants contributors to understand the project purpose, setup instructions, and usage guidance immediately.

Which file should be prioritized?

Options.reason: Incorrect. CODEOWNERS assigns review responsibility.
Incorrect. SECURITY explains how to report vulnerabilities.
Incorrect. A code of conduct defines community behavior expectations.
Correct. A README introduces the repository and provides essential usage information.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: A README is the primary entry point for understanding a repository.

questions.Question:
A team wants a repository visible to anyone on the internet.

Which visibility should they choose?

Options.reason: Correct. Public repositories are visible to everyone.
Incorrect. Private repositories restrict access to selected users and teams.
Incorrect. Internal repositories are visible within an enterprise where supported.
Incorrect. Archived repositories are read-only and not a visibility category for public access.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Public visibility is used when a repository should be openly accessible.

questions.Question:
A team wants to preserve a meaningful point in history for version 1.0 without changing the files.

Which Git concept should they use?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Branch protection controls changes to important branches.
Incorrect. Labels categorize issues and pull requests.
Correct. A tag marks a specific commit, commonly for versions.
Incorrect. Project views organize work items.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Tags are commonly used to identify release versions or notable commits.

questions.Question:
A team wants to use GitHub.dev for quick browser-based edits but needs a full cloud development environment with compute and terminal access for larger work.

Which feature should they use for the larger work?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Pages hosts static websites.
Correct. Codespaces provides a cloud-hosted development environment with compute resources.
Incorrect. Sponsors supports funding open-source maintainers.
Incorrect. Insights provide repository activity and analytics.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Codespaces is appropriate when browser editing is not enough and a configured development environment is required.

questions.Question:
A team repeatedly creates repositories with the same starter structure, labels, and common files.

Which repository feature should they use?

Options.reason: Incorrect. A star bookmarks or highlights interest.
Incorrect. A fork copies a repository for independent contribution.
Incorrect. Watching controls notifications.
Correct. A template repository helps create new repositories from a predefined structure.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Repository templates help standardize new repositories.

questions.Question:
A project requires explicit terms explaining how others may use, modify, and distribute the code.

Which file is most appropriate?

Options.reason: Correct. A LICENSE file states the legal terms for using the project.
Incorrect. README explains usage and setup guidance.
Incorrect. CONTRIBUTING explains how to contribute.
Incorrect. CODEOWNERS defines review ownership.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: A LICENSE file communicates the project license terms.

questions.Question:
A team needs GitHub to automatically request reviews from the platform team when infrastructure files change.

Which repository file supports this?

Options.reason: Incorrect. SECURITY explains vulnerability reporting.
Incorrect. README provides project overview.
Correct. CODEOWNERS maps files or paths to required owners for review.
Incorrect. SUPPORT explains how to get help.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: CODEOWNERS helps route review responsibility for specific paths.

questions.Question:
A repository owner wants to define expectations for external contributors, including how to propose changes and run tests.

Which file should be added?

Options.reason: Incorrect. LICENSE defines usage rights.
Correct. A CONTRIBUTING file documents contribution guidelines.
Incorrect. Dependabot configuration manages dependency update behavior.
Incorrect. Release notes summarize shipped changes.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: CONTRIBUTING guidance improves consistency for incoming contributions.

questions.Question:
A maintainer wants to publish packaged version notes and downloadable artifacts for version 2.1.

Which GitHub feature should be used?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Discussions support community conversations.
Incorrect. Projects track work items.
Incorrect. Actions secrets store sensitive automation values.
Correct. Releases package versioned software and notes from repository history.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Releases are used to distribute versioned project outputs.

questions.Question:
A repository owner wants a high-level view of repository activity such as contributors, commits, and traffic.

Which feature area should they review?

Options.reason: Correct. Insights provide repository metrics and activity views.
Incorrect. Gists share code snippets.
Incorrect. Sponsors supports maintainer funding.
Incorrect. Packages hosts package artifacts.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Repository Insights help owners understand repository activity and health.

questions.Question:
A developer wants to create a personal copy of an open-source repository under their own account before proposing changes back.

Which action should they perform?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Archiving makes a repository read-only.
Incorrect. Deleting removes repository access and history from GitHub.
Correct. Forking creates a copy under another account for independent changes.
Incorrect. Transferring issues does not create a working copy.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Forks are commonly used for open-source contribution workflows.

questions.Question:
A team wants to prevent accidental direct changes to the default branch and require review before merge.

Which capability should they configure?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Topics improve discoverability.
Correct. Branch protection can require pull requests, checks, and restrictions before changes are merged.
Incorrect. Pages publishes static content.
Incorrect. Git LFS stores large files outside normal Git object storage.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Branch protection helps enforce quality and review controls for important branches.

questions.Question:
A developer has completed work on a feature branch and wants teammates to review the changes before merging.

Which GitHub feature should they use?

Options.reason: Incorrect. A milestone groups issues and pull requests by target.
Incorrect. A wiki stores project documentation.
Incorrect. Secret scanning detects exposed secrets.
Correct. A pull request supports review, discussion, checks, and merging.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Pull requests are central to collaborative code review in GitHub.

questions.Question:
During a review, a teammate wants to request specific changes before a pull request can be merged.

Which review outcome should they choose?

Options.reason: Correct. Request changes records that updates are required before approval.
Incorrect. Closing a project does not review code.
Incorrect. Starring does not affect pull request review status.
Incorrect. Creating a release publishes a version, not review feedback.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Pull request reviews can approve, comment, or request changes.

questions.Question:
A support team wants to track bugs and enhancement requests in a repository.

Which GitHub feature should they use?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Git tags mark commits.
Incorrect. Codespaces provides development environments.
Correct. Issues track tasks, bugs, enhancements, and discussions tied to work.
Incorrect. Dependabot alerts identify vulnerable dependencies.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Issues are the primary GitHub feature for tracking work and feedback.

questions.Question:
A community wants long-form conversations and Q&A that are not necessarily tied to a specific bug or code change.

Which feature is best?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Pull requests focus on proposed code changes.
Correct. Discussions support community conversations, questions, and announcements.
Incorrect. Rulesets enforce repository policies.
Incorrect. Artifacts store workflow outputs.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Discussions are suited for broader collaboration and community engagement.

questions.Question:
A maintainer wants to categorize issues as bugs, documentation, or enhancements.

Which feature should they use?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Releases publish versions.
Incorrect. Forks create repository copies.
Incorrect. SSH keys authenticate Git operations.
Correct. Labels classify and filter issues and pull requests.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Labels provide lightweight categorization for issues and pull requests.

questions.Question:
A team wants to group issues and pull requests for a specific product launch target date.

Which GitHub feature should they use?

Options.reason: Correct. Milestones group issues and pull requests around a goal or target.
Incorrect. Gists share snippets.
Incorrect. Topics improve repository discovery.
Incorrect. Mobile supports collaboration from devices.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Milestones are useful for tracking progress toward a release or objective.

questions.Question:
A user receives too many alerts and wants to control which repository activities generate notifications.

Which configuration should they review?

Options.reason: Incorrect. License usage relates to billing and seats.
Incorrect. The dependency graph lists dependencies.
Correct. These settings control how and when GitHub sends updates.
Incorrect. Branch comparison compares code changes.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub notifications and subscriptions help users manage collaboration signals.

questions.Question:
A reviewer wants to leave feedback on a specific changed line in a pull request.

Which capability should they use?

Options.reason: Incorrect. A star bookmarks the repository.
Correct. Line comments attach feedback to specific code changes.
Incorrect. A project field stores planning metadata.
Incorrect. An environment secret stores sensitive workflow values.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Line-level pull request comments make feedback precise and actionable.

questions.Question:
Fabrikam wants a repeatable cloud development environment that can be launched from a repository with predefined tools.

Which feature should the platform team recommend?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Discussions are for conversations.
Incorrect. Sponsors helps fund maintainers.
Incorrect. Pages hosts static websites.
Correct. Codespaces provides hosted development environments that can use repository configuration.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Codespaces supports standardized development environments in the cloud.

questions.Question:
Fabrikam wants to automate build and test tasks whenever code is pushed or a pull request is opened.

Which GitHub feature should be configured?

Options.reason: Correct. GitHub Actions automates workflows triggered by repository events.
Incorrect. A wiki stores documentation.
Incorrect. Desktop is a GUI client.
Incorrect. Mobile supports collaboration from devices.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Actions is used for CI/CD and event-driven automation.

questions.Question:
A workflow must run on compute provided by GitHub without maintaining company servers.

Which runner type should be used?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Self-hosted runners are managed by the customer.
Incorrect. Topics classify repositories.
Correct. GitHub-hosted runners provide managed compute for workflow jobs.
Incorrect. Project templates standardize planning views.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub-hosted runners reduce infrastructure management for workflow execution.

questions.Question:
Fabrikam needs workflow configuration stored as code inside the repository.

Which file format is commonly used for GitHub Actions workflow files?

Options.reason: Incorrect. CSV stores tabular data.
Correct. GitHub Actions workflows are commonly defined using YAML files.
Incorrect. PNG is an image format.
Incorrect. PDF is a document format.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Actions workflows are defined in YAML files in the repository.

questions.Question:
A developer wants AI-assisted autocomplete-style coding suggestions in the editor.

Which GitHub product provides this capability?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Pages publishes static sites.
Incorrect. Projects tracks work.
Incorrect. Packages hosts package artifacts.
Correct. GitHub Copilot provides AI-assisted coding suggestions.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Copilot assists with coding by suggesting code and related content.

questions.Question:
Fabrikam wants to check source code for potential vulnerabilities using semantic analysis in GitHub.

Which capability should be used?

Options.reason: Correct. Code scanning can use CodeQL to detect security issues in code.
Incorrect. Stars show interest in repositories.
Incorrect. Issue forms collect structured issue data.
Incorrect. Branch comparison shows differences between branches.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Code scanning helps identify security issues in code and can be powered by CodeQL.

questions.Question:
A team needs to store a password for a workflow without placing it in source code.

Which GitHub feature should be used?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Labels categorize work items.
Incorrect. Badges display status or metadata.
Correct. Secrets store sensitive values for workflows.
Incorrect. Topics improve discoverability.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Actions secrets help keep sensitive workflow values out of repository code.

questions.Question:
A workflow should deploy only after a pull request is merged into the main branch.

Which trigger design best matches this requirement?

Options.text: Run the workflow only on issue comment events.
Options.reason: Incorrect. Issue comments do not represent merged source changes.

Options.text: Run the workflow on push events to the main branch.
Options.reason: Correct. A merge to main results in a push to that branch, which can trigger the workflow.

Options.text: Run the workflow only when a repository is starred.
Options.reason: Incorrect. Star events do not represent a deployment-ready change.

Options.text: Run the workflow only when a milestone is closed.
Options.reason: Incorrect. Milestones are planning objects, not source merge events.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Using a push trigger scoped to main aligns deployment with merged changes.

questions.Question:
Fabrikam wants a flexible planning board that can show issues and pull requests by status, owner, and iteration.

Which feature should be used?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Packages hosts artifacts.
Incorrect. Pages hosts static websites.
Incorrect. Sponsors funds maintainers.
Correct. GitHub Projects supports flexible planning views and custom fields.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Projects helps teams plan and track work across issues and pull requests.

questions.Question:
A team wants project items automatically moved based on issue or pull request activity.

Which Projects capability supports this?

Options.reason: Correct. Project workflows can automate item updates based on events.
Incorrect. Archive makes a repository read-only.
Incorrect. Secret scanning detects exposed secrets.
Incorrect. A tag marks a commit.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Projects includes automation workflows for managing project item state.

questions.Question:
A product owner wants to view the same project work as a table and as a board.

Which Projects concept enables this?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Forks copy repositories.
Incorrect. SSH keys authenticate access.
Correct. Views present project items in different layouts and filters.
Incorrect. Releases publish software versions.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Project views let teams represent the same data in different formats.

questions.Question:
A team wants to store planning metadata such as priority, size, and target iteration for project items.

Which GitHub Projects capability should they use?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Topics classify repositories.
Correct. Custom fields capture structured planning metadata.
Incorrect. Code owners map files to reviewers.
Incorrect. Themes style static sites.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Custom fields make project tracking more structured and adaptable.

questions.Question:
A manager wants to measure progress across project items without leaving GitHub Projects.

Which capability is most relevant?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Git blame shows commit attribution for lines.
Incorrect. Git LFS handles large files.
Incorrect. Gists share snippets.
Correct. Project insights provide charts and visibility into project progress.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Project insights help teams understand status and delivery trends.

questions.Question:
Adventure Works wants users to sign in with stronger protection than only a password.

Which approach should be recommended?

Options.reason: Correct. Two-factor authentication adds an additional verification factor.
Incorrect. Topics classify repositories.
Incorrect. Discussion categories organize conversations.
Incorrect. Project views organize work tracking.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Two-factor authentication improves account security by requiring an additional factor.

questions.Question:
Adventure Works needs to grant repository permissions to groups of users rather than assigning access one person at a time.

Which organization feature should be used?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Labels categorize issues and pull requests.
Incorrect. Releases publish versioned outputs.
Correct. Teams group organization members for permissions and collaboration.
Incorrect. Gists share snippets.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Teams simplify permission management within GitHub organizations.

questions.Question:
A repository contains a supported package manifest, and the owner wants visibility into dependencies and related security alerts.

Which feature area should be enabled or reviewed?

Options.reason: Incorrect. These features publish static websites.
Correct. These features provide dependency visibility and vulnerability notifications.
Incorrect. These features reflect interest and notification preferences.
Incorrect. These features organize planning work.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Dependency graph and Dependabot alerts help maintainers understand and respond to dependency risk.

questions.Question:
Adventure Works wants GitHub to detect committed tokens and credentials in repositories.

Which capability should be used?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Issue templates standardize issue creation.
Incorrect. Sponsors supports maintainer funding.
Incorrect. A wiki stores documentation.
Correct. Secret scanning helps detect exposed secrets in repository content.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Secret scanning is used to help identify leaked secrets.

questions.Question:
A security team wants clear instructions for reporting vulnerabilities privately.

Which repository file should they add?

Options.reason: Correct. A SECURITY file explains how to report vulnerabilities and supported versions.
Incorrect. README introduces the project.
Incorrect. LICENSE defines project usage terms.
Incorrect. CODEOWNERS assigns review responsibility.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: A SECURITY file improves vulnerability reporting and response clarity.

questions.Question:
An organization needs to define what members can do across repositories and administrative areas.

Which concept is most relevant?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Markdown tables format text.
Incorrect. Topics improve discovery.
Correct. Roles and permissions determine allowed actions in GitHub.
Incorrect. Git aliases shorten local Git commands.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub administration relies on appropriate roles and permissions.

questions.Question:
A developer wants to authenticate Git operations over SSH from a trusted workstation.

Which credential type is appropriate?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Labels categorize work items.
Correct. SSH keys can authenticate Git operations to GitHub.
Incorrect. Project fields store planning metadata.
Incorrect. Releases package versions.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: SSH keys are commonly used for secure Git authentication.

questions.Question:
A repository should be made read-only because active development has ended, but its history must remain visible.

Which action should the owner take?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Deleting removes the repository instead of preserving it read-only.
Incorrect. Forking creates a copy but does not freeze the original.
Incorrect. Starring does not change repository state.
Correct. Archiving makes the repository read-only while preserving it.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Archiving is appropriate when a project is no longer maintained but should remain accessible.

questions.Question:
An enterprise wants a policy-oriented approach that can enforce rules consistently across repositories.

Which capability is most relevant?

Options.reason: Correct. Rulesets help enforce repository policies such as branch and tag rules.
Incorrect. Gists share snippets.
Incorrect. Footnotes format documentation.
Incorrect. Sponsor tiers define funding options.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Rulesets provide a centralized way to apply repository governance rules.

questions.Question:
Adventure Works wants to make expectations for respectful participation clear to external contributors.

Which file should be added?

Options.reason: Incorrect. CODEOWNERS routes review ownership.
Incorrect. Dependabot configuration manages dependency updates.
Correct. A code of conduct defines expected community behavior.
Incorrect. Artifacts store workflow outputs.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: A CODE_OF_CONDUCT file supports healthy and inclusive community participation.

questions.Question:
A maintainer wants to show that the repository welcomes contributions and explain suitable first tasks.

Which practice best supports this goal?

Options.reason: Incorrect. This reduces collaboration channels.

Options.text: Use contributor guidance and helpful issue labels.
Options.reason: Correct. Guidance and labels such as beginner-friendly categories help new contributors participate.

Options.text: Require every contributor to be an organization owner.
Options.reason: Incorrect. This is excessive and inappropriate for community contribution.

Options.text: Store all documentation outside the repository only.
Options.reason: Incorrect. This makes contribution guidance harder to discover.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Clear contribution guidance and well-organized issues help grow a healthy community.

questions.Question:
A developer finds a useful open-source repository and wants to save it to revisit later while also signaling interest.

Which GitHub action should they use?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Archiving is controlled by owners and makes a repository read-only.
Incorrect. Transferring changes repository ownership.
Incorrect. Branch protection enforces merge rules.
Correct. Starring bookmarks a repository and can signal interest.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Stars are commonly used to bookmark and discover repositories.

questions.Question:
A company wants to encourage internal teams to collaborate using open-source practices within the organization.

Which concept describes this approach?

Options.reason: Correct. InnerSource applies open-source collaboration practices inside an organization.
Incorrect. Secret scanning detects exposed credentials.
Incorrect. Git LFS handles large files.
Incorrect. Pages publishes static sites.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: InnerSource uses open collaboration patterns for internal software development.

questions.Question:
An open-source maintainer wants community members to ask questions, share ideas, and propose improvements without opening code changes.

Which GitHub feature best supports this?

Options.reason: Incorrect. Actions cache improves workflow performance.
Incorrect. SSH certificate authorities help authenticate SSH access.
Correct. Discussions provide a forum-like space for community conversation.
Incorrect. Release assets distribute versioned files.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Discussions are well suited for community Q&A, announcements, ideas, and general collaboration.
